chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Muhammad ibn Mudarib said:
I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the eunuch, does he effect divorce? He said, 'He does not effect divorce.'

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (Imam Ali al-Rida, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: Does a eunuch have the right to divorce his wife according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that a eunuch (*al-khasi*) does not possess the legal capacity to effectuate a divorce (*talaq*). This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes between the physical ability to consummate marriage and the legal authority to dissolve it, often contrasting with views that might equate sterility with incapacity to divorce. The concise answer reflects the precision of the Imams in defining the boundaries of marital rights and responsibilities.
